title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：lunch　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 lunch 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1975 the cook ① served the lunch that no worker in the canteen would have recorded, and he said the serving was the whole of the day. The ② lunch, meaning the meal itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed unrecorded in the book; a lunch, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ lunch in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ lunch at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A lunch, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the cook said the recording is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the lunch was the whole of the matter, meaning the break and not the meal. The ⑥ lunch, meaning the break and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; lunch, he said, is either something you serve or the only word that means both a meal and a break. He said the break is the part they remember.

By 1980 the ⑦ lunch had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ lunch of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of recording; lunch, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ lunch I remember is the meal recorded in the menu, which closed in 1982 and is still recorded as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ lunch, my mother said in 1984, is the only meal that improves by being recorded; every lunch, she said, is a break that has agreed to look like a meal. She said the break was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 午餐；午饭（指食堂里每一顿旁边的那一顿）
B. n. 午餐；午饭（指那顿午饭本身，与碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：serve the lunch 端上这一顿午饭
D. n. 午餐；午饭（指留给孩子们分的那一碗那一顿）
E. n. 午饭之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的午饭之事）
F. n. 午餐；午饭（指菜谱里写到、被记载的的那一顿）
G. n. 歇息、滋味（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 滋味（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: served the lunch that no worker in the canteen would have recorded
The lunch, meaning the meal itself and not the bowl
the lunch at the far table
the lunch was the whole of the matter
the lunch had become a line in a menu
The lunch of the whole thing
A lunch, my mother said in 1984

answers.why: serve the lunch 意为“端上这一顿午饭”，1975 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位工人肯记载的一顿午饭做了一遍。
lunch 意为“午餐；午饭”，指那顿午饭本身而不是碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记载。
lunch 意为“午餐；午饭”，指食堂里每一顿旁边的那一顿，每一顿旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
lunch 意为“午餐；午饭”，指最远那张桌角留给孩子们分的那一碗那一顿，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
lunch 意为“歇息、滋味”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份歇息就是那件事的全部。
lunch 意为“滋味”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那顿午饭，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
lunch 意为“午餐；午饭”，指菜谱里写到、被记载的的那一顿，到 1980 年这一顿成了菜谱里的一行。
lunch 意为“午饭之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的午饭之事是一处食堂和三个日子的记载。
lunch 意为“午餐；午饭”，我记得的是菜谱里记载过的那一顿，1982 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一顿。
lunch 为抽象总称，母亲 1984 年说，午饭是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的午饭。
